extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/formatting standards for preparing, presenting, and entering amendments to patent applications (claims, drawings, specification) and the Office procedures for handling non-compliant amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim status identifiers and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim must be presented with a status identifier indicating its status (e.g., (Original), (Currently amended), (Canceled), (Withdrawn), (Previously presented), (New), (Not entered), (Withdrawn-currently amended)). Claims present on the international filing date or rectified pursuant to PCT Rule 91 must have the status identifier (original); claims amended or added under PCT Article 19 or 34 with effect in the U.S. national stage must have (previously presented); claims canceled pursuant to PCT Article 19 or 34 with effect in the U.S. national stage must have (canceled). If the amendment in the U.S. national stage application makes a change in a claim, use (currently amended) for that claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the status identifiers used are incorrect but the amendment otherwise places the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter the non-compliant amendment and correct incorrect status identifiers via an examiner's amendment. The Office will accept certain alternative identifiers (see Acceptable Alternatives list) if the status is accurate and clear. When accepting alternatives, the examiner need not notify applicant or require corrective amendment; the examiner need not state on the record that alternatives were accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings to show changes in amended claims
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims being currently amended must be presented with markings to indicate changes relative to the immediate prior version. Changes must be shown by strike-through (deleted matter) or underlining (added matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two exceptions: (1) for deletion of five or fewer consecutive characters, double brackets may be used (e.g., [[eroor]]); (2) if strike-through cannot be easily perceived (e.g., deletion of number “4” or certain punctuation), double brackets must be used (e.g., [[4]]). As an alternative to double brackets, extra portions of text may be included before and after text being deleted, all in strike-through, followed by including and underlining the extra text with the desired change (example given: number 4 as number 14 as). An accompanying clean version is not required and should not be presented. Only claims with status “currently amended” or “withdrawn” will include markings. Any claims added by amendment must be indicated as “new” and the text of the claim must not be underlined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim text submission requirements when amending
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of all pending claims under examination and withdrawn claims must be submitted each time any claim is amended. Pending claims not being currently amended, including withdrawn claims, must be presented in clean version (no markings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any claim presented in clean version constitutes an assertion that it has not been changed relative to the immediate prior version except to omit markings. A canceled claim must be indicated as “canceled” and the text must not be presented. Canceled and not-entered claims must be listed only by claim number and status identifier, without presenting text. When applicant submits text of canceled or not-entered claims, the Office may accept it if otherwise compliant with 37 CFR 1.121 to reduce processing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim numbering and ordering rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims in each amendment paper must be presented in ascending numerical order. The original numbering of claims must be preserved throughout prosecution; when claims are canceled, remaining claims must not be renumbered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consecutive canceled or not-entered claims may be aggregated into one statement (e.g., Claims 1–5 (canceled)). A canceled claim can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number. When adding new claims after canceling original claims, the new claims must be numbered consecutively beginning with the number next following the highest numbered claim previously presented, in compliance with 37 CFR 1.126.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable alternative status identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent delays, the Office will waive certain provisions and accept alternative status identifiers not specifically set forth in 37 CFR 1.121(c) if the status of the claims is accurate and clear. Examples map the official identifiers to acceptable alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided mapping examples: 'Original' → 'Original Claim'/'Originally Filed Claim'; 'Currently amended' → 'Presently amended'/'Currently amended claim'; 'Canceled' → 'Canceled without prejudice'/'Cancel'/'Canceled herein'/'Deleted'; 'Withdrawn' → 'Withdrawn from consideration'/'Withdrawn – new'/'Withdrawn claim'; 'Previously presented' → 'Previously amended'/'Previously added'/'Previously submitted'; 'New' → 'Newly added'/'New claim'; 'Not entered' → 'Not entered claim'. Office personnel may accept additional variations if clear. If alternative identifiers are accepted, applicant will not be notified and corrective amendment is not required; examiner need not note acceptance on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing amendment submission and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes to application drawings must comply with 37 CFR 1.84 and be submitted on a replacement sheet (for changes) or a new sheet (for additions). The replacement sheet must be identified in the top margin as 'Replacement Sheet' and the new sheet as 'New Sheet.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The replacement drawing sheet must include all figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is amended. The figure(s) of the amended drawing(s) must not be labeled 'amended.' A marked-up copy of any amended drawing figure showing the changes may be included; it must be clearly labeled 'Annotated Sheet' and presented in the amendment or remarks section that explains the change. An explanation of changes must be presented in the 'Amendments to the Drawings' or remarks section. If changes are not approved, applicant will be notified in the next Office action and must amend the brief and detailed description sections of the specification to be consistent with drawing changes. The proposed drawing correction practice has been eliminated; do not submit changes in red ink. Replacement drawings without markings (in compliance with 37 CFR 1.84) are required. Drawing submissions without specification or claims amendments after allowance should be forwarded to the Office of Patent Publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendments: authority and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.121(g) permits the Office to make amendments to the specification, including claims, by examiner's amendments without paragraph/section/claim replacement to expedite prosecution and reduce cycle time. Examiner's amendments may add or delete subject matter by instructions to make changes at precise locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a non-compliant amendment would otherwise place the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter it and provide an examiner's amendment to correct non-compliance (e.g., incorrect status identifier). The examiner may (A) provide a claim listing with proper identifiers in an examiner's amendment, (B) print the claim listing, cross out improper identifiers and write in correct ones as an attachment, or (C) correct improper identifiers by instructions in an examiner's amendment. The examiner's amendment should include why the amendment was non-compliant and indicate how it was corrected. Authorization from applicant or attorney/agent and extensions are not required if changes are non-substantive (formatting/typographical). Authorization and appropriate extensions are required if the examiner's amendment is substantive (e.g., cancellation of a claim or scope change); authorization must be given within the time period for reply set forth in the last Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant amendment notification and required corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment submitted on or after July 30, 2003 fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.121, the Office will notify applicant by Form PTOL-324 (Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment) identifying which section is non-compliant, items required for compliance, and reasons (e.g., missing status identifiers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTOL-324 enumerates common defects (amended paragraphs without markings; abstract not on separate sheet; drawings not properly identified; missing complete claim listing; missing text for pending claims; improper/missing status identifiers; claims not in ascending order). The notice indicates what corrected material is required and prescribes time periods for reply depending on amendment type. Consequences for failure to reply vary by amendment type and can include non-entry of the amendment or abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods and handling by amendment type
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office's required reply periods and consequences differ by amendment type when a notice of non-compliance is issued:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from MPEP: (A) Preliminary amendment filed after filing date: TSS notice with 30 days or one month (whichever later), no extensions; failure -> examined without entry of preliminary amendment; reply must include corrected section. (B) Preliminary amendment present on filing date: OIPE notice with 2-month reply period; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) available; failure -> abandonment. (C) Non-final amendment including RCE: TSS notice 30 days or one month; extensions available under 1.136(a); failure -> abandonment. (D) After-final amendment: forwarded unentered to examiner; notice provides no new time; applicant must still reply to final Office action to avoid abandonment; corrected entire amendment must be submitted if resubmitting. (E) Supplemental amendment when no suspension: forwarded to examiner; not entered as a matter of right. (F) Supplemental amendment within suspension: TSS notice 30 days or one month, no extensions; failure -> examined without entry. (G) Amendment filed in response to Quayle action: TSS notice 30 days or one month; extensions available; failure -> abandonment. (H) After-allowance amendment under 37 CFR 1.312: forwarded to examiner; not entered as matter of right; examiner may attach Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment to Form PTO-271; if resubmitting corrected after-allowance amendment, entire corrected amendment must be submitted before payment of issue fee. Also: amendments adding claims beyond paid-for number must be accompanied by excess claims fees or will be non-entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of non-compliance (abandonment and non-entry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely respond to a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment can result in abandonment of the application or non-entry of the amendment depending on amendment type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: abandonment occurs if failure to reply to notices for non-final amendments or amendments filed in response to Quayle actions; non-entry occurs for preliminary amendments or supplemental amendments when applicable. The PTOL-324 notice explains the applicable consequences and available time periods/extensions (if any).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments when directions are defective
rubrics_metrics.description: Directions for the entry of an amendment may be defective (e.g., inaccurate paragraph number/page/line or lack of precision). If the correct place of entry is clear from context, the amendatory paper will be properly entered in the Technology Center and a notation, initialed by the examiner, will be made on the margin of the amendatory paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the next Office action, the applicant should be informed of the alteration in the amendment and the entry as thus amended. The examiner assumes full responsibility for the change. Non-entry may occur where defective directions and context leave doubt as to applicant's intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of replacement paragraphs/sections (amendment of amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a replacement paragraph or section of the specification is to be amended, it should be wholly rewritten and the original insertion canceled. A marked-up version of the replacement paragraph/section should be presented using underlining for added subject matter and strike-through for deleted subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matter canceled by amendment can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the canceled matter as a new insertion. A claim canceled by amendment (deleted in entirety) may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and other papers filed in the application must be signed by: (1) a registered patent attorney or patent agent of record appointed in compliance with § 1.32(b); (2) a registered attorney or agent not of record acting in a representative capacity under § 1.34; (3) an assignee as provided under § 3.71(b); or (4) all applicants unless an assignee of the entire interest has acted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unsigned or improperly signed amendment is not entered. When an unsigned or improperly signed amendment is received it will be listed in the application file but not entered; the examiner will notify applicant and advise to furnish a duplicate properly signed amendment or ratify the amendment. In an application not under final rejection, a 1-month time period is given to ratify the previously filed amendment (37 CFR 1.135(c)). An amendment signed by the applicant in an application with an attorney/agent of record should be entered and acted upon, with copies sent both to the attorney and directly to the applicant, noting 'Copy to applicant.' An amendment signed by a person removed from the register of attorneys/agents will not be entered and the file submitted to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment definition, effect on original disclosure, and publication format
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment is one received on or before the mail date of the first Office action (37 CFR 1.115). For applications filed on or after Sept 21, 2004, a preliminary amendment present on the filing date is part of the original disclosure; for earlier filings it is part of original disclosure only if referred to in the first executed oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A preliminary amendment filed after filing date is not part of original disclosure. If a preliminary amendment is in a format that cannot be included in the patent application publication, OIPE will issue a notice requiring a substitute specification in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(b)(3) and 1.125. The only usable format for an amendment to the specification (other than claims) for publication is a substitute specification in compliance with those rules. Applicants should submit references to prior applications in an Application Data Sheet (ADS) under 37 CFR 1.76 rather than in a preliminary amendment. Preliminary amendments to claims or abstract compliant with 1.121(c) or 1.121(b)(2) include complete claim listings or replacement abstracts and can be published as submitted. There is no need to file a preliminary amendment to claims on filing; making the claim set part of the originally filed specification may avoid paying an application size fee, as both specification and preliminary amendment are used in counting pages for 37 CFR 1.16(s). A preliminary amendment filed with a national stage entry (35 U.S.C. 371) is not part of the original disclosure because it was not present on the international filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that preliminary amendments comply with 37 CFR 1.121
rubrics_metrics.description: Any preliminary amendment, regardless of filing time, must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 (e.g., include a complete listing of all claims and each section of the amendment must begin on a separate sheet). Preliminary amendments in a transmittal letter will not comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a preliminary amendment filed after filing date fails to comply, applicant will be notified (e.g., Notice to File Corrected Application Papers) requiring a substitute specification if amendment amends the specification. Failure to file the required substitute specification will be treated as incomplete reply with no new time period for reply.
